hero.headline: Learn anything, grounded in your reading.
hero.subhead: Seed a topic with the sources you trust, and an AI author writes you an interactive course — lesson by lesson, as you learn.

how.heading: A course that’s written as you learn it

seed.title: Seed a course
seed.body: Give it a title, say why you’re learning, and upload the reading you trust — a handbook, a scripture, your own notes.

author.title: An AI author gets writing
author.body: It studies your sources and publishes your first lesson — an interactive page written from your reading, never over it.

advance.title: Learn, ask, advance
advance.body: Finish a lesson and the next one is written for you. The course unfolds at your pace, as far as you want to take it.

features.heading: Built for real study, not a feed of videos

grounded.title: Grounded in your reading
grounded.body: Your uploaded resources are the syllabus. Lessons are written from them and never trust ungrounded knowledge over them.

interactive.title: Interactive lessons
interactive.body: Every lesson is a self-contained interactive page — reading, worked examples, and quizzes that check you actually got it.

ask.title: Ask anything
ask.body: Stuck mid-lesson? Ask right there. The author reads your question and replies inline, in the lesson where you asked it.

references.title: References that stay current
references.body: Alongside lessons you get living cheat-sheets — glossaries and key facts the author revises as your understanding deepens.

language.title: In any language
language.body: Turn a course into a full edition in another language — the same lessons, re-authored, not machine-glossed. Switch any time.

share.title: Share & public links
share.body: Share a course with someone by email — read-only or with editing rights — or mint an anonymous public link anyone can open.

mocks.heading: What a lesson actually looks like
mocks.body: Not a video to sit through. A page written from your sources, with the questions — and the answers — in the same place you were reading.

lesson.title: A lesson, written from your reading
lesson.body: Prose, worked examples and pull-outs, assembled from the sources you uploaded and never over them.

quiz.title: Questions that check you got it
quiz.body: Short checks inside the lesson, marked as you go, so you find the gap before you move past it.

ask.title: Ask where you got stuck
ask.body: Your question is answered inline, in the lesson where you asked it — not in a forum you'd have to go find.

faq.heading: Questions, answered.
faq.q1: Is the course written by AI, or by a person?
faq.a1: By AI, and we won't pretend otherwise. What makes it different is what it's allowed to use: your uploaded sources are the syllabus, and a lesson is written from them rather than from whatever the model happens to remember. If it isn't in your reading, it doesn't go in the lesson.
faq.q2: What do I need to upload?
faq.a2: Whatever you'd have studied anyway — a handbook, a scripture, a set of lecture notes, your own writing. One source is enough to start, and you can add more as the course goes on.
faq.q3: Do I get the whole course at once?
faq.a3: No. The first lesson is written when you seed the course, and the next when you finish the last. That's deliberate: the author sees what you got right and what you asked about before it writes what comes next.
faq.q4: Can I learn in a language other than English?
faq.a4: Yes. A course can be turned into a full edition in another language — the same lessons re-authored, not machine-glossed — and you can switch between editions whenever you like.
faq.q5: Can I share a course with someone else?
faq.a5: Three ways: by email as a read-only viewer, by email with editing rights, or as an anonymous public link anyone can open without an account.
